title: Energy sources and scientific advances
summary: Learn about fossil, renewable and nuclear energy, green chemistry and nanotechnology.
cards.0.p: Sources that renew themselves quickly are called renewable. Sun, wind, rivers and geothermal (underground heat) are among them. Coal, oil, natural gas and uranium are nonrenewable. Electricity is not a source but an energy carrier.
cards.0.etk.soru: Put each one in the right group.
cards.0.etk.ogeler.7.2: Its reserves are limited. Nuclear fuel counts as nonrenewable.
cards.0.etk.ogeler.8.2: Electricity is produced from another source. It is not a source itself.
cards.0.etk.ogeler.9.2: It is not found free in nature. It is produced by using energy.
cards.0.key: Hydrogen is an energy carrier too. Nuclear energy releases no CO₂, but it is not renewable, because uranium reserves are limited.
cards.0.once.soru: Is the electricity you get from an outlet an energy source?
cards.0.once.secenekler.0.neden: Electricity is produced from another source and carries the energy.
cards.0.once.secenekler.1.neden: Electricity itself is not a source. What matters is what it was made from.
cards.0.once.secenekler.2.neden: Electricity can be made from coal or from sunlight. So it is a carrier, not a source.
cards.1.h: Fossil fuels and the oil refinery
cards.1.p: Coal formed from buried plants, and oil and natural gas from plankton, over millions of years. Crude oil is separated by boiling point through fractional distillation.
cards.1.key: Small molecules leave from the top of the tower. Natural gas is mostly methane. Coal and oil can contain sulfur.
cards.2.h: Combustion, CO₂ and the greenhouse effect
cards.2.p: Every fossil fuel gives CO₂ when it burns. CO₂ absorbs the infrared rays given off by Earth's surface and warms the atmosphere. This is called the greenhouse effect. Extra CO₂ strengthens this effect and leads to global warming.
cards.2.svg#14: if O₂ is short: CO + soot
cards.2.key: If O₂ is short, toxic CO and soot form. The natural greenhouse effect is necessary for life. Per unit mass, CH₄ is much stronger than CO₂.
cards.3.p: When the sulfur in fuel burns, SO₂ forms, and in the air this gas turns into H₂SO₄. Nitrogen oxides also give HNO₃. So the pH of rain drops below 5.6. This rain wears away marble and acidifies lakes.
cards.3.svg#18: prevention: flue gas desulfurization, catalytic converter
cards.3.key: Removing sulfur from power plant smokestacks and using catalytic converters in vehicles prevents this.
cards.4.p: A solar cell turns light directly into electricity. A solar collector heats water instead. A wind turbine turns the kinetic energy of moving air into electricity with a generator. Neither releases CO₂.
cards.4.svg#7: Both are intermittent: storage is needed at night and in still air
cards.4.key: Electricity from sun and wind depends on the weather. That is why batteries and storage matter.
cards.4.once.soru: What does a rooftop solar collector with black pipes produce?
cards.4.once.secenekler.0.neden: The collector uses the sun's heat to warm the water in its pipes.
cards.4.once.secenekler.1.neden: Solar cells produce electricity. A collector only heats.
cards.4.once.secenekler.2.neden: Hydrogen is produced by electrolysis. A collector only heats water.
cards.5.p: In hydroelectric power, the potential energy of water behind a dam turns a turbine. Geothermal power uses hot water and steam from underground. Wave and tidal power plants use the motion of the sea.
cards.5.svg#14: Iceland, Kenya and Indonesia lead in geothermal
cards.5.key: Cooled geothermal water is pumped back underground. Dams count as emission-free, but they affect river ecosystems.
cards.5.once.soru: At a dam, which energy of the water is turned into electricity?
cards.5.once.secenekler.0.neden: Water stored up high turns the turbine as it falls.
cards.5.once.secenekler.1.neden: Dam water is not heated. The energy of falling water is used.
cards.5.once.secenekler.2.neden: The water does not react. The energy that comes from its height is used.
cards.6.p: Biomass is matter of living origin, such as wood, crop waste and manure. Bioethanol comes from sugar, biodiesel from vegetable oil, and biogas from waste that rots without oxygen.
cards.6.svg#13: biogas: made by bacteria without oxygen
cards.6.key: Plants take in CO₂ as they grow, so the CO₂ released by burning is partly balanced. Still, biofuel is not fully carbon neutral, and it competes with food for farmland.
cards.6.once.soru: Farm animal manure is left to rot in a closed tank. Which fuel comes out?
cards.6.once.secenekler.0.neden: Waste that rots without oxygen gives biogas, which is mostly methane.
cards.6.once.secenekler.1.neden: Gasoline is made from crude oil.
cards.6.once.secenekler.2.neden: The gas from rotting manure is mostly methane.
cards.7.p: In a nuclear power plant, the fission of 235U nuclei produces heat. This heat turns water into steam, and the steam turns a turbine. Spent fuel stays radioactive for thousands of years.
cards.7.key: Fusion is the Sun's energy source, but there is no commercial fusion power plant yet. The Chernobyl (1986) and Fukushima (2011) accidents showed how important safety is.
cards.7.once.soru: How does a nuclear power plant produce electricity?
cards.7.once.secenekler.0.yazi: Heat makes steam, steam turns a turbine
cards.7.once.secenekler.0.neden: The heat of fission boils water, and the steam turns a turbine.
cards.7.once.secenekler.1.neden: Electricity directly from light happens in a solar cell.
cards.7.once.secenekler.2.neden: Uranium does not burn. Its nuclei split (fission).
cards.8.p: In a fuel cell, H₂ and O₂ react without burning. Chemical energy turns directly into electricity, and the only product is water. But hydrogen is not found free in nature and has to be produced.
cards.8.key: Hydrogen is produced by electrolysis or from natural gas. It counts as clean only if it is made with renewable electricity. This is called green hydrogen.
cards.9.p: Sustainability means meeting today's needs without using up the options of future generations. A carbon footprint is the total greenhouse gas emissions of a person or a product.
cards.9.svg#8: Other greenhouse gases such as CH₄ are added as CO₂ equivalents
cards.9.key: Every step from raw material to waste counts. First use less energy, then get the rest from low-carbon sources.
cards.9.once.soru: How should you travel 1 km to school to have the smallest carbon footprint?
cards.9.once.secenekler.1.neden: A car burns gasoline and releases CO₂.
cards.9.once.secenekler.2.neden: A taxi is also a car and burns fuel.
cards.10.p: Green chemistry aims to prevent pollution from the start. To do this, it avoids creating waste, seeks high atom economy and uses safe solvents. Atom economy shows how much of the reactants' atoms end up in the product.
cards.10.key: Even at 100% yield, a by-product counts as waste. The caffeine in coffee is removed with supercritical CO₂ instead of a toxic solvent.
cards.11.p: 1 nm is 10−9 m. At sizes of 1-100 nm, the surface-to-volume ratio grows and most atoms are on the surface. So the material reacts more readily and makes a good catalyst.
cards.11.key: Graphene and nanotubes are nanomaterials. Nanosilver kills germs. Nano TiO₂ in sunscreen blocks ultraviolet rays. Gold nanoparticles look red.
cards.12.p:
• Fossil fuels and uranium are nonrenewable, and sun and wind are renewable.
• Combustion gives CO₂ (greenhouse effect), and sulfur gives SO₂ (acid rain).
• Nuclear power plants use 235U fission and leave waste.
• A fuel cell makes electricity from H₂ and O₂.
• Green chemistry prevents waste. At the nanoscale, the surface-to-volume ratio grows.
quiz.0.q: Order the steps by which the sulfur in coal turns into acid rain.
quiz.0.e: When sulfur burns, SO₂ forms. In the air, O₂ oxidizes SO₂ to SO₃. In clouds, SO₃ gives H₂SO₄ with water, and the pH of rain drops below 5.6.
quiz.1.q: Quicklime is made from limestone: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂. If the desired product is CaO, what is the atom economy in percent? (Atom economy = molar mass of desired product / molar mass of reactants × 100; Ca = 40, C = 12, O = 16)
quiz.1.e: The molar mass of CaCO₃ is 100 g/mol, and that of CaO is 56 g/mol. The atom economy is 56 / 100 × 100 = 56%. The remaining 44% leaves as waste CO₂.
quiz.2.q: Match each technology with where it gets its energy.
quiz.2.e: A photovoltaic cell turns light into electricity, a wind turbine the kinetic energy of air, and a hydroelectric plant the potential energy of falling water. A fuel cell makes H₂ and O₂ react without burning. A nuclear power plant uses the heat of <sup>235</sup>U fission.
quiz.3.q: Which statement about hydrogen and fuel cells is true?
quiz.3.o.0: Hydrogen is a primary energy source found free and in large amounts in nature.
quiz.3.o.1: A fuel cell burns hydrogen and makes heat first, then electricity.
quiz.3.o.2: Hydrogen gas is easy to store.
quiz.3.o.3: The only product of a fuel cell is water.
quiz.3.e: Hydrogen is an energy carrier produced from water or natural gas by using energy. A fuel cell turns chemical energy directly into electricity without burning. Storing hydrogen gas requires high pressure or deep cooling.
quiz.3.y.0: In nature, hydrogen is mostly found in compounds and is produced by using energy. So it is a secondary source.
quiz.3.y.1: A fuel cell does not burn hydrogen. It turns chemical energy directly into electricity.
quiz.3.y.2: Hydrogen gas has little energy per volume. So it must be compressed or cooled, which makes storage hard.
A:ozet: Distill crude oil and compare the CO₂ emissions of fuels. Remove the greenhouse gases, watch acid rain and explore power plants. Finally, calculate atom economy and nano surface area.
A:adimlar.0.metin: Crude oil is heated at the bottom of the tower. As the vapor rises, it cools, and each molecule condenses on the tray that matches its boiling point. This is called fractional distillation. Choose a molecule that will go into gasoline.
A:adimlar.0.gorev.ipucu: Gasoline is taken from the upper part of the tower and is made of small molecules.
A:adimlar.0.gorev.tamam: Gasoline is made of molecules of about C₅–C₁₀. The smaller the molecule, the lower its boiling point and the higher up the tower it condenses.
A:adimlar.1.metin: When a fossil fuel burns completely, CO₂ and water form. Make the same heat (1 MJ) with three fuels and find the one that releases the least CO₂.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.ipucu: Look for the fuel with the shortest bar.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.tamam: Natural gas (mostly methane) is the fossil fuel that releases the least CO₂. Still, its emissions are not zero, because natural gas is also a fossil fuel.
A:adimlar.2.metin: Now we will remove all the greenhouse gases from the atmosphere.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.soru: What happens to Earth's average temperature?
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: The incoming sunlight stays the same, but the heat given off escapes to space without being held back. So the surface cools.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: The infrared rays given off by the surface escape to space without being held back. The average temperature drops from about 15 °C to −18 °C.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: Greenhouse gases hold heat in. Removing them causes cooling, not warming.
A:adimlar.3.metin: Increase the amount of SO₂ in the air. Watch the pH of the rain and the marble.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.soru: Why is the pH of unpolluted rain ≈ 5.6 and not 7?
A:adimlar.3.gorev.secenekler.0.yazi: SO₂ in the air acidifies all rain
A:adimlar.3.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: Even without SO₂, the pH of rain is 5.6. SO₂ pushes the pH below 5.6 and causes true acid rain.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: Basic substances would raise the pH. Rain is slightly acidic.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.secenekler.2.yazi: It dissolves CO₂ from the air
A:adimlar.3.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: CO₂ forms H₂CO₃ with water, and this weak acid lowers the pH to about 5.6. SO₂ gives strong H₂SO₄, so it lowers the pH even more.
A:adimlar.4.metin: Each power plant turns one type of energy into electricity. A fuel cell makes electricity directly from H₂ and O₂. Select the plants one by one and look at the conversion chain.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.soru: Which ones make electricity without a turbine and generator?
A:adimlar.4.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: In a solar cell, light sets electrons in the semiconductor moving directly. In a fuel cell, H₂ and O₂ react at the electrodes. Neither has a spinning part.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: Both use the energy of motion to turn a turbine, and a generator produces the electricity.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: The solar cell is right, but a nuclear plant uses the heat of fission to make steam and turn a turbine.
A:adimlar.5.metin: Atom economy shows how much of the reactants' atoms end up in the desired product. We can make ethanol by three different routes. Find the route with 100% atom economy.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.ipucu: Look for the reaction that makes no by-product.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.tamam: In the addition reaction, all the reactants' atoms end up in ethanol, and the atom economy is 100%. The substitution route stays at 31% because of the NaBr waste.
A:adimlar.6.metin: Cut the cube into smaller cubes and triple the total surface area.
A:adimlar.6.gorev.ipucu: Cutting each edge into 2 pieces doubles the surface area.
A:adimlar.6.gorev.tamam: You got 27 small cubes, and the total surface area tripled. A material with a larger surface-to-volume ratio reacts more readily. That is why nanoparticles are good catalysts.
A:kapanis.0: Crude oil is separated into its parts by fractional distillation. Small molecules leave from the upper part of the tower.
A:kapanis.1: For the same heat, natural gas gives the least CO₂, but it is still a fossil fuel.
A:kapanis.2: Without the greenhouse effect, the average temperature would be about −18 °C. Extra CO₂ strengthens this effect.
A:kapanis.3: The pH of clean rain is about 5.6. SO₂ and nitrogen oxides push it even lower.
A:kapanis.4: Solar cells and fuel cells make electricity without a turbine. Other power plants use a turbine and a generator.
A:kapanis.5: Green chemistry prevents waste from the start. At the nanoscale, the surface-to-volume ratio grows.
